column1: # --randtour high sweep {20,30,40} + pure-proportional wsample. Seeds 801-1000, 900s.
# The {10,14,20} sweep showed ntil-45 plateaus from randtour 10->20 (t10~=t20
# on solves; t20 has a modest flip-efficiency edge; the t14 dip was noise).
# ntil-43 still improved monotonically to t20, so the uniform-draw tournament
# may not have saturated there yet -- push the randtour axis higher to {20,30,
# 40} and see where it finally turns over.
# 4th config is the weighted-proportional sampler (--wsamplepow=1) at
# randtour=1: a single draw with probability proportional to ddfw weight, taken
# directly -- pure proportional, no tournament. This is wsample's natural form
# (the draw is already biased toward heavy sources, so it doesn't need the
# R*K-sample-then-top-K tournament to find them). Tests "is proportional
# sampling alone good enough?" against the uniform-draw tournament rows.
# (--wsamplepow=0 = off = uniform; =1 linear; =2 quadratic ...) randk default 1.
# NOTE: --wsamplepow=1 --randtour=1 is now the compiled default, so the t-rows
# below pin --wsamplepow=0 explicitly to stay uniform-draw tournaments (the
# original comparison). ws1 reproduces the new weighted-proportional default.
# name
ws1
